answer: Quadratic identity pricing: an agent pays 1 unit for its first identity, and each further identity from the same funding cluster pays the next square, 4, 9, 16. Why it works: the marginal clone soon costs more than the value of its marginal vote, so a rational attacker quits. Summing squares, 100 clones cost about 338,000 units against 100 for honest users, a 3,000-fold-plus asymmetry; even 20 clones already pay 2,870. Seen through that prism, every bulk-registered key becomes a relic, and because the fee curve is carved in marble on-chain, no operator can quietly soften it.
